q: The law of excluded middle (LEM) and axiom of choice (AC) in HoTT: both are consistent with HoTT (they hold in the set-theoretic model) but not provable. LEM for mere propositions states: for any P: Prop, ‖P‖ + ‖¬P‖. In HoTT without LEM:
opts: There exist propositions P that are neither provably true nor provably false — HoTT is constructive by default
exp: HoTT is constructive: LEM is not provable from the type-theoretic axioms alone (it is consistent but not derivable). Adding LEM gives a 'classical' version of HoTT. Without LEM, existence proofs must be constructive (providing actual witnesses), and the propositional truncation ‖P‖ separates existence from explicit witnesses.
